lens: Whether every identifier the manuscript and its build artifacts print resolves to a record in this repository, whether the committed builds (especially the Qeios .docx) are built from this pin, whether the repository's statements about its own deposit are true at this commit, and which of those statements an instrument actually reads.
what_i_read: research/manuscripts/tests/ (all 90 modules extracted; read in full: test_journal_references_match_the_prose.py, test_aso_deposition_doi_is_one_fact.py, test_the_word_manuscript_is_current_and_whole.py, test_the_deposit_the_papers_cite_is_current.py, test_the_archive_contains_every_paper_the_builder_builds.py, test_the_submission_uploads_are_individual_files.py, test_a_display_item_cell_is_not_clipped.py, test_the_preprint_record_reads_the_paper_it_deposits.py)
central_claim: Every identifier this manuscript and its committed builds print - 23 numbered references and their PMIDs/DOIs, the Zenodo deposition DOI, the ORCID, the two RRIDs, every named oligonucleotide sequence, and the table and figure numbers - resolves to a record in this repository; the .docx that the Qeios v2 post consumes is built from this exact commit; and the repository's own statements about what is deposited where are true at this commit.

blockers.summary: The two records that tell the author what to do before posting Qeios v2 both state that the Zenodo draft is current with this tree. At this commit it is not: the tree moved after the refresh and neither record was updated, and the checklist's act list therefore says 'publish' with no instruction to refresh first.
blockers.quote: fusion-junction-aso-preprint-checklist.md, section '3-i': "\u2705 **THE DRAFT IS REFRESHED AND CURRENT WITH THE TREE (2026-08-29).** Dispatched `deposit-zenodo.yml` with `new_version=false` at `f6e313d98` (Actions run 33279143126)." and, four paragraphs later, "1. **Publish the Zenodo version, by hand** \u2014 <https://zenodo.org/deposit/22166420>. Irreversible". deposit-state.json says the same thing: "\u2b50 THE DRAFT IS NOW CURRENT WITH THIS TREE: refreshed 2026-08-29 ... It no longer is."
blockers.evidence: Measured at the pin, no network. deposit-state.json `pending.uploaded_manifest_digest` = bb5655ba9f1afbc4cf74df41af98177cad9c3106e36419b13ec4ddf4bfb9902c, taken at `pending.uploaded_at_git_revision` = f6e313d98 (2026-08-29 22:39 UTC). fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json at the pin carries `archive_content_digest` = eff1258052fbd97462a119e4a99ab2b505f7906b0a4a8054ba331ce104ea15ec at `git_revision` 9bd466fac (2026-08-30 00:30 UTC). The two digests differ, so the draft is behind the tree. Diffing the manifests' own 483-path inventories between f6e313d98 and the pin returns exactly one changed file: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-cover-letter.md, rewritten at 9bd466fac ('round 19's cover-letter blocker'). I independently re-hashed all 483 manifest entries against the pin: 0 mismatches, so the manifest is current and the draft is the stale side. Log: s20-citations-log.txt.
blockers.why_a_reader_would_be_misled: trimcrae is the only person who can perform the Zenodo publish, it is irreversible, and both records he would consult tell him the draft already matches the tree. Acting on them freezes a published archive whose cover letter is one revision behind the repository - the same 'publish a draft that is already behind' failure the guard file test_the_deposit_the_papers_cite_is_current.py was written to prevent, one commit later. The correct instruction at this pin is: dispatch deposit-zenodo.yml with new_version=false again, then update uploaded_manifest_digest, then publish.
blockers.artifact: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-preprint-checklist.md (section 3-i) and research/manuscripts/aso/deposit-state.json (pending._uploaded_fields_mean). NOT the Qeios .docx - these are the instruction records for the act this review gates.

p1s.summary: Nothing reads the reference list inside the .docx that Qeios consumes. The one instrument that checks printed reference numbering against the prose reads a different artifact (the two-column journal PDF), and the .docx's own gate asserts only floors that a lost reference section would clear.
p1s.evidence: test_journal_references_match_the_prose.py::test_the_printed_pdf_numbers_the_references_as_the_prose_cites_them opens `pdf = os.path.join(MANUSCRIPTS, "aso", "fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.pdf")` - the journal PDF only. test_the_word_manuscript_is_current_and_whole.py asserts existence, stamp non-collision, source-hash freshness, embedded-vs-linked images, and `measured` floors of words>=500, headings>=4, images>=1. test_the_submission_uploads_are_individual_files.py's content check is parametrized over build_submission_parts.PARTS, which is exactly {'title-page','figure-legends'} - not the manuscript .docx. I verified the .docx IS correct today: 23 entries under numId 1, abstractNum lvl0 `w:start=1` `numFmt=decimal`, in the prose's first-citation order, 22 doi.org hyperlink targets (ref 6 has no DOI upstream either), and the builder's own counts reproduce the stamp exactly (words 5525, headings 19, images 1). The .docx and the PDFs share one HTML pipeline (build_submission_docx.py imports build_submission_pdf.assemble), and this repository has already shipped the defect where an HTML <ol> renumbered from 1 in the built artefact while the markdown was correct.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any change to how the references splice or how LibreOffice numbers the <ol> - a second numbered list earlier in the body sharing numId 1, a converter upgrade, a change to the References anchor - would renumber or drop the .docx reference list with the stamp still matching, the floors still clearing, and the PDF gate still green over a different file. A Qeios reader following superscript 8 would land on the wrong paper.
p1s.artifact: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article-manuscript.docx (the Qeios v2 deliverable); gap is in research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_word_manuscript_is_current_and_whole.py

p1s.summary: The guard that is supposed to warn the publisher when the Zenodo draft is stale is satisfied, at this pin, by the sentence asserting the draft is NOT stale.
p1s.evidence: test_the_deposit_the_papers_cite_is_current.py::test_a_pending_draft_still_matches_the_tree_it_was_built_from takes the non-matching branch here (bb5655ba != eff125805) and then asserts `re.search(r"re-?run the deposit|new_version=false|refresh the draft", section, re.I)` over section 3's slice. I replicated the exact logic on the committed checklist: it matches, and the matching token is `new_version=false` inside "\u2705 **THE DRAFT IS REFRESHED AND CURRENT WITH THE TREE (2026-08-29).** Dispatched `deposit-zenodo.yml` with `new_version=false` at `f6e313d98`" - a past-tense report that the refresh already happened, i.e. the opposite of the instruction the assertion's own failure message demands ('nothing in the preprint checklist tells whoever publishes it to refresh the draft first'). The guard's own comment anticipates a weaker version of this ('the refresh instruction could be demoted to a superseded, retained note further down'); the token surviving inside a completed-status line is one level past what it was hardened against. Log: s20-citations-log.txt.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: It is already satisfied vacuously. Any future refresh followed by any commit that touches a deposited file reproduces the same green: the completed-status sentence keeps the regex satisfied forever, so the gate can never fire again unless someone deletes that sentence. A phrase match cannot distinguish an instruction from a report that the instruction was already carried out; the check needs to key on the recorded digest rather than on prose.

p1s.summary: The archive manifest's promise-to-file mapping checks its quoted promises against the extended report only, so the journal article's own Data availability wording is bound to nothing.
p1s.evidence: aso_archive_manifest.py line 72: `PAPER = os.path.join(ASO, "fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md")`, and the `_promise_still_in_manuscript` flag on every promise row is computed as `_promise_text_found_in_paper(paper, row.get("quote", row["promise"]))` against that one file. The journal article's Declarations says "All code, graded artefacts, per-design tables, every screen's parameters and the complete bounds on each claim are deposited under [DOI]" and "the complete correction record is released with the archive" - wording that appears in no promise row's `quote`. Of the tests that touch the archive, test_the_archive_contains_every_paper_the_builder_builds.py checks only that each citing paper, its built PDFs and their stamps are inside the manifest; test_aso_archive_manifest_vocabulary.py checks junction-label vocabulary and on-disk agreement; test_aso_deposition_doi_is_one_fact.py checks the DOI string. None reads the journal article's promise nouns.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Editing the journal article's Data availability to promise something the archive does not carry - a new artefact class, a supplementary file, a raw-sequence bundle - would leave every gate green, because the only mechanism that asks 'you said X is released, where is it?' re-reads the extended report. The manifest's `gaps.promises_resolving_to_no_file` would stay empty because the new promise never became a row.

p2s.summary: PROCESS DISCLOSURE, not a finding. A repository-wide `git grep` for the RRIDs returned two lines from research/autonomy/review-seats/ - blinded material for this same seat id. I did not open those files and issued only path-scoped greps afterwards, but I can no longer claim independence on the question those lines concerned (whether any instrument reads the RRIDs), so I have deliberately omitted that question from my findings rather than report a contaminated one.
p2s.evidence: The grep was `git grep -n "CVCL_C6M" <pin> -- research`; two of the returned lines were file paths under research/autonomy/review-seats/ with inline match text. All later greps were scoped to research/manuscripts and excluded redteam files. Log: s20-citations-log.txt.

p2s.summary: The manuscript's Data availability cites a DOI that does not resolve at this commit. This is the repository's declared reserve-then-rebuild ordering rather than a text defect, but it is a hard precondition on the act this review gates and it is stated nowhere in the manuscript itself.
p2s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md: "are deposited under [doi:10.5281/zenodo.22166420](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22166420), the citable record for them." deposit-state.json records 22166420 only under `pending` (drafted 2026-08-29, `_what_remains`: "Publishing, by hand, on Zenodo"). The cover letter at the same commit states the reading: "every archive link in both papers currently resolves to nothing", measured by `record=verify` (Actions run 33279967090) which "answered `404 ... exactly what a RESERVED but unpublished DOI does`". deposit-state's `_what_remains` names the ordering: Zenodo publish first, Qeios v2 second.
p2s.artifact: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md and the .docx built from it (both print the DOI); state recorded in research/manuscripts/aso/deposit-state.json

p2s.summary: The preprint checklist contradicts the cover letter about whether the article's DOIs resolve, in the same commit.
p2s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-preprint-checklist.md section 3a: "With the archive published, every DOI in the condensed article resolves, and the paper is graded inside every one of the venue's limits, the submission is unblocked today." fusion-junction-aso-cover-letter.md, same commit: "So every archive link in both papers currently resolves to nothing." Section 3a's sentence was true of 10.5281/zenodo.22061075 and the papers were re-pointed at 22166420 on 2026-08-29; it was not revised. The checklist's own section 3-i states the rule this breaks: "a claim of the form 'the diff is empty' is a MEASUREMENT WITH A DATE".

p2s.summary: A deposited artifact states a reason for not naming the third design that the manuscript no longer gives, and that the manuscript's own Test articles section contradicts.
p2s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-reagent-coverage.json: `if_a_third_published_breakpoint_were_added.why_it_is_not_named_in_the_papers` = "It carries no test article: none of the five in the ASO papers' section 4 spans EWSR1 exon 13 to NR4A3 exon 3, so naming it would put a reagent in front of a laboratory with nothing to test it in." (hard-coded at aso_reagent_coverage.py line 191). The journal article at the pin says instead: "It is not named for synthesis: this junction is third by reported prevalence and the selection takes the first two", and its Test articles section says "On that reading USZ20-EMC1 carries EWSR1 exon 13 joined to exon 3 - the third design named above". The checklist section 3-ii records the manuscript-side correction ('It is stated in section 2 now') and the generated artifact was not revised with it. This JSON is inside the archive the manuscript's Data availability points at (verified against the manifest's 483-path inventory).

p2s.summary: The archive carries three .docx build stamps and no .docx. A reader who downloads the deposit gets records describing files that are not there.
p2s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json contains fusion-junction-aso-journal-article-manuscript.docx.build-stamp.json, -figure-legends.docx.build-stamp.json and -title-page.docx.build-stamp.json, and its `payload_file_types.by_extension` census lists json/py/md/pdf/png/svg/csv/fasta/sh with no .docx entry at all. deposit-state.json relies on this: "the Word build stamps are themselves deposited files, so rebuilding them moved the archive digest". No manuscript sentence promises the .docx is in the deposit, so this is an orphan record rather than a broken promise.

p2s.summary: DEFECT IN A DIFFERENT DELIVERABLE, openly tracked. Table 1's last column is clipped mid-word in the two-column journal PDF and the anonymized PDF. The Qeios .docx is unaffected.
p2s.evidence: Text extracted from the committed PDFs at the pin: fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.pdf prints "seam reagent margin WT gap duplex (bp) \u0394Tm floor (\u00b0C) test a ... \u2265 26.6 E-N, engin const ... \u2265 36.0 T-N*, engin const"; -anonymized.pdf is identical. The preprint and manuscript PDFs and the .docx all print "test article", "E-N, engineered construct" and "T-N*, engineered construct" in full (counts measured: 'engineered construct' 4/4/4 in .docx, preprint and manuscript PDFs vs 2/2 in the journal and anonymized PDFs). This is not an unnoticed defect: test_a_display_item_cell_is_not_clipped.py names it as AUT-PD-188, scopes a strict=True xfail to exactly those two builds, and records that fixing it costs a seventh page against a six-page budget. It belongs to the journal-submission act, not to the Qeios v2 post.

p2s.summary: The manuscript's front matter carries a last_verified date five commits stale. It is stripped from every build, so it reaches no reader of the Qeios .docx.
p2s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md front matter: `date: 2026-08-20` / `last_verified: 2026-08-22`. The file was edited at 473413bdf, f8cba4bb2, 445169e83, 9338d6178, 86c68dfbb, 656ff2a29 and 558c3eef4 between 2026-08-27 and 2026-08-29. The front matter's own text says "This block is stripped from the PDF builds and reaches no reader of the submitted article", and the extracted .docx confirms it: the document begins at the H1.

p2s.summary: CLEAN, recorded because it is the bulk of what this seat checked. Every identifier in the manuscript and its builds resolved.
p2s.evidence: All 24 citation sites in the manuscript pair equal-length number and PMID lists; every superscript resolves to an entry; every one of the 23 entries is cited; every entry carries the PMID its citation names; first-citation order is exactly 1..23. All 23 PMIDs were fetched from PubMed and every author segment matched journal-reference-authors.json's `rendered` field character-for-character, every journal abbreviation matched journal-abbreviations.json, and no title, year, volume or page range disagreed with the fetched record (only case differences in two DOIs, 10.1158/1078-0432.ccr-12-2715 and 10.1200/po.22.00039, which resolve identically). Printed reference numbering equals the cited set in the journal, preprint and anonymized PDFs and in the .docx. All six build stamps' `built_from` digests match the committed sources at this pin, including both figure rasters, and the .docx stamp's `measured` block reproduces exactly under the builder's own counting. Every named sequence - both reagents, both controls, the third design, the condemned one-base slide and both exon-2 reagents - resolves to exactly one row of fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv with the parent-duplex length, gene and margin the paper prints, and the panel arithmetic (190 designs, 176 distinct sequences, 9 matching more than one junction, 38 junctions, five partners) reproduces from that CSV. The Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22166420 is the manifest's, is printed in the .docx and in three PDFs, is correctly absent from the anonymized build, and no trace of the superseded 22061075 survives in any paper. One ORCID exists repository-wide. Both RRIDs are anchored in fusion-junction-aso-data-sources.json.
